note: MEASURED COST FINDING, from The Sexton first gate run under the new instrumentation. Decision 0130 channel work (de367cb7, render the whole flow tree not the top 6.7%) added +467 CPU-s across 9 lab-calibration and vessel-session tests, and made hearth_population_calibration the SLOWEST TEST IN THE WORKSPACE at 187 s -- 2.3x the previous maximum of 82.9 s, up from 9.6 s. Verified not contention: identical across three full-gate runs at different loads, and 89 s measured alone in nextest. It went unnoticed because make ci had run 9 times against make gate 368. Nothing is broken and nothing needs reverting -- the cost may well be worth what the wider flow tree buys -- but if you own that area you should know the number. Reading rule worth keeping: in a baseline re-record, a broad uniform shift across UNRELATED tests is the machine; a local shift concentrated in RELATED tests is the code. This diff had both at once (-637 CPU-s uniform, +467 local) and reporting only one half would have misattributed the other.
